audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer phases[N].side read "Skill" while content win[0..6] and packet.levelChart both read Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Mel. All seven rows disagreed between the two layers.
audit.why: Mel is immobile with no dash and no escape; Neeko's Tangle-Barbs into Blooming Burst out-trades her whenever Rebuttal is spent, and Pop Blossom lands on her at 6. The late flip is real: Golden Eclipse is global (25000 range) and hits every Overwhelm mark, and Radiant Volley out-ranges Neeko at 950.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides brought onto the content values, with each row's why and rating rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why asserted a "3-second knockup" the kit does not give, and no phase why named a real cooldown.
audit.why: The spike map here is Rebuttal's cooldown (38/35/33/29/26) against Neeko's own windows, and the late flip is Golden Eclipse at 120/100/80 plus Radiant Volley falling to 6 seconds at rank 5.
audit.corrected: Invented duration removed; the level 3 and level 6 rows now key off Rebuttal's 38-second rank-1 cooldown, and the late row off Mel's range and global ult.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single decisive interaction of this lane was never stated: Rebuttal reflects projectiles, and BOTH of Neeko's laning spells are projectiles — Blooming Burst and Tangle-Barbs. Poking into a lit Rebuttal returns Neeko's own root and damage to her while Mel takes none. Also missing: Mel's passive Overwhelm stacks into a genuine execute (Riot's text says the stacks are consumed to execute), and Golden Eclipse reaches every marked target from anywhere on the map.
audit.why: Both Neeko Q and E carry the projectile flag in the kit, and Riot's Rebuttal text says it reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker and prevents her taking damage. That is the whole reason this lane has a cast-timing rule at all.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, tradeBad, dontsFull[0].d, enemyWin, breakdown.late and winCon.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions claims Rebuttal denies Pop Blossom's dash via a "terrain" flag.
audit.why: Riot's own description of Rebuttal is a barrier around herself that reflects projectiles, prevents damage and grants move speed — nothing about terrain or blocking dashes. Per the rule that the description outranks a misfiring derived flag, I wrote no dash-denial claim. What I did write is what the text supports: Pop Blossom into an active Rebuttal deals no damage to her.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d and breakdown.mid now key the R commit to a spent Rebuttal without asserting a dash block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's own defect line is right: 46.81% over 141 games sits badly against a chart that gives Neeko six of seven stages.
audit.why: Both the packet levelChart and the content layer say Neeko wins early, so I did not fight them — but the late row deserves a much heavier weighting than the rest of the page gave it.
audit.corrected: Left the sides as the two agreeing sources have them; pushed the two-plus-items rating to 8/10 and made breakdown.late, breakdown.carry and ahead all say the same thing — this lead has an expiry date.

notes: CHART: all seven full-layer sides read "Skill" while content win[0..6] and packet.levelChart agreed on Neeko x6 then Mel. I brought the full layer onto the agreeing pair, so no content win[N] edit was needed, and rewrote every phases[N].why and rating in the same proposal. PACKET DEFECT ACKNOWLEDGED: the packet flags that 46.81% over 141 games sits badly against Neeko taking six of seven stages. I did not overrule two agreeing sources on the early rows, but I weighted the late row to 8/10 and made breakdown.late, breakdown.carry, ahead and loading all repeat that the lead expires — see questionsForUser for whether the middle rows should move. DIFF FIELD: diff="EVEN" / diffRating="5.5/10" / breakdown.difficulty do not match a sub-50% win rate; I did not guess a token for the diff enum. KIT FLAG MISFIRE: Rebuttal carries a derived "terrain" flag and missingInteractions therefore claims it denies Pop Blossom's dash. Riot's description is a barrier around herself that reflects projectiles, prevents damage and grants move speed — no terrain, no dash block — so I asserted only that Pop Blossom into an active Rebuttal does no damage. PRONOUNS: fourteen full-layer fields called Mel "he/his"; all fixed. The content layer was already correct. LEFT ALONE: breakdown.feeding, breakdown.spikes, report[6..10], report[12], report[14] and the entire content layer, which was already Mel-specific and correctly gendered.
